title: Implementation notes — Canonical Brain, confidential access, and offline capture
subtitle: CUT-G2 execution started · 2026-09-19 23:09 CDT
intro: Each item is a decision, deviation, or tradeoff made during implementation. Acknowledge if fine. Discuss to write what should change. Revert to flag for undo.

groups.label: OSS-G2 — Persist and project effective privacy

items.title: Derive the durable Brain ID from the Portable tenant ID

body.Spec said: Use a placement-independent durable Brain ID, but did not choose its encoding.
body.What I did: Froze the ADR 0014 role-distinct brn_ Base32 re-encoding of the existing canonical tenant_<uuid>.
body.Why: It is deterministic, one-to-one, portable, and avoids adding a second persisted identity.
body.Risk: Malformed or noncanonical tenant IDs now fail closed instead of receiving a generated replacement.

items.title: Separate issuer epoch from authorization generation

body.Spec said: Bind stationary issuer authority and generation-changing consent without conflating them.
body.What I did: Reserved issuer_epoch for commit authority and authorization_generation for grant, consent, and launcher-policy changes; existing control_epoch and fencing_epoch retain their meanings.
body.Why: Each value has a different lifecycle and invalidation boundary.
body.Risk: Later migrations must remove ambiguous serialized epoch names without reinterpreting existing storage fields.

items.title: Bind legacy epochs to exact Portable artifacts
items.where: ADR 0018, Portable Brain v5 and legacy issuer evidence

body.Spec said: Assign pre-cutover commits to a legacy epoch without rewriting historical payloads or digests.
body.What I did: Defined append-only evidence by normalized manifest path, optional JSONL ordinal, exact payload SHA-256, and positive issuer_epoch.
body.Why: The active product has no single generic commit identity across every historical family.
body.Risk: Portable v5 migration must enumerate every declared artifact and row exactly once.

items.title: Bind the final admitted tier in the receipt

body.Spec said: Keep offline delivery immutable while binding the tier that the canonical Brain finally admits.
body.What I did: The request digest covers the requested tier and the rest of the immutable envelope. The terminal receipt separately binds the final admitted tier.
body.Why: The sender cannot know the server's final admission decision when it creates the request digest.
body.Risk: Every dequeue path must verify the full receipt binding before removing a body.

items.title: Keep malformed input inside closed error boundaries
items.where: Consent, launcher-policy.v1, and outbox.v1 contract tests

body.Spec said: Malformed consent, startup policy, and delivery evidence must fail closed.
body.What I did: Added adversarial cases for mutable mappings, Unicode surrogates, malformed runtime state, and invalid typed values, then normalized every failure to its contract error.
body.Why: Leaking implementation exceptions makes fail-closed behavior dependent on the caller.
body.Risk: Persistence and transport adapters added in later phases must preserve the same boundaries.

items.title: Make admission and rollback behavior explicit before implementation
items.where: Fixed decisions and public Phases 4 through 6

body.Spec said: Offline delivery and remote capture must remain bounded, destination-bound, and receipt-safe under failure.
body.What I did: Added canonical size/rate/concurrency/writer-queue/storage limits, durable enqueue success, non-evicting outbox_full behavior, and explicit new-ID destination conversion to the implementation gates.
body.Why: A bounded envelope alone does not define behavior under server pressure, local capacity exhaustion, crash boundaries, or rollback to another destination.
body.Risk: OSS-G4 through OSS-G6 cannot pass until the implementation and crash/admission tests prove these requirements. Existing OSS-G1 value-contract tests remain valid but do not claim queue storage or server admission implementation.

items.title: Expose a zero-loss receipt-protection boundary
items.where: Fixed decisions and public Phases 4 through 6

body.Spec said: The owner selected the architecture in which client body-removal receipts wait for independently durable protection.
body.What I did: Added a transport-neutral receipt-protection finalizer, a stable recovery_pending result, acknowledgement binding, idempotent protection replay, and outbox crash tests that retain the body until a protected terminal receipt arrives.
body.Why: A locally durable commit can otherwise be lost with its primary host after the client has already deleted the only replayable body.
body.Risk: This expands OSS-G4 through OSS-G6. The private deployment must still prove that its independent failure domain meets the required synchronous latency and availability before cutover.
